producer_report.summary:
I redid the CI caches so the athena binary key, the `setup --ci` skip digest and a policy test all read one list. The list is `BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS` in `xtask/src/main.rs`: crates/**, xtask/**, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md. Prompts and docs/system-facts.md are therefore in both the key and the digest, which was the major finding of the rejected job. I ran `cargo test -p xtask` (all pass) and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`. `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. I did not run the full `cargo test --locked`.

- **xtask:**
  - `inputs_digest` hashes OS, architecture, then each file's path and length-prefixed content, in path order.
  - `xtask build-inputs` prints the globs.
  - `can_skip_build` is true only with `--ci`, an adopted binary file and a stamp equal to the digest.
  - `rebuild_stamped` removes the stamp, builds, and writes the stamp only on success. Every non-skip build goes through it, so a later non-CI or failed build leaves no stale stamp.
  - `build_and_adopt` now skips or rebuilds through these.
  - A comment and a printed line say the skip runs before the dirty-tree refusal.
  - The gitleaks version check from the rejected candidate is kept.
- **ci.yml:**
  - All nine athena-bin keys (six restores, three saves) now use the nine globs. The restore steps for gitleaks and the athena binary sit before 'Set up' in fmt, clippy, test, history, attribution and pr-head. There are no restore-keys.
  - The saves are in fmt, clippy and test shard 0, with the existing default-branch condition and `cache-hit != 'true'`.
  - Every `uses:` line is still pinned by a 40-character SHA.
  - The header comment states what the key covers and does not cover, the older-commit effect, the dirty-tree note, and that history, attribution and pr-head restore only. It also says the speed-up is not measured here.
- **policy.rs:**
  - New `job_text_in` and `job_steps_in` work on a given ci.yml text.
  - `compiled_in_files()` scans `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` literals in production code under crates/ and xtask/, plus the manifests and setup.sh.
  - `check_athena_bin_keys` requires each key to hash exactly the `build-inputs` output and to cover every scanned file.
  - `check_restore_before_setup` runs on all six jobs.
  - Mutant tests (a glob removed, docs/system-facts.md removed, an uncovered file, a restore removed or moved after setup) must be rejected, and the real file must pass.
  - A new test checks the 40-character SHA pin on every `uses:` line.
- **CHANGELOG:** one Unreleased entry for both caches, their keys, the globs, the stamp and skip, the older-commit effect, and that the speed-up is not measured here.

checks_run.note: First run: 52 unit tests, 20 ci_shards, 10 fingerprint tests passed. One new policy mutant test failed because its extra path sat under crates/ (covered by crates/**). I fixed the test.
17 passed, including the boundary-word scan, the new key-coverage, restore-order and mutant tests, and the SHA-pin test. Run again after the fix.
Printed the nine globs, in the same order as the ci.yml hashFiles lists.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml: every athena-bin cache key (all restore and save steps) uses hashFiles covering crates/**, xtask/**, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md. In each of the fmt, clippy and test jobs, actions/cache/restore steps for gitleaks and the athena binary come before the step named 'Set up (pinned toolchain, gitleaks, athena)'.
criteria_check.evidence: All nine athena-bin key lines in ci.yml now read hashFiles('crates/**', 'xtask/**', 'rust-toolchain.toml', 'Cargo.toml', 'Cargo.lock', 'athena.toml', 'defaults.toml', 'setup.sh', 'docs/system-facts.md'). `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` passes athena_bin_keys_cover_every_compiled_in_file (checks each key line) and every_job_restores_the_tool_caches_before_it_runs_the_setup_step (restore before setup in fmt, clippy, test, history, attribution and pr-head).

criteria_check.criterion: ci.yml has matching actions/cache/save steps with the existing condition (not a pull request, ref equal to the default branch, no exact cache hit). Every uses: line is pinned by a 40-character SHA. History, attribution and pr-head also restore before setup, or a comment states why they do not. No other workflow behavior changes.
criteria_check.evidence: The save steps in fmt, clippy and test (shard 0 for test) keep the condition: not a pull request, DEFAULT_BRANCH_ONLY, and cache-hit != 'true'. The policy test every_job_restores_... asserts this, and every_action_is_pinned_by_a_full_commit_sha passes. History, attribution and pr-head restore before setup, with comments saying they restore only. The ci_shards tests pass, so the shard, needs and timeout layout is unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: xtask has one shared list of athena build inputs that both the skip digest and the policy test read. The comment in ci.yml and the CHANGELOG do not claim more than the key covers.
criteria_check.evidence: BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS in xtask/src/main.rs is read by input_files/inputs_digest and printed by `xtask build-inputs`, which policy.rs runs through CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask. The ci.yml comment and the CHANGELOG entry list the same nine globs. They say CHANGELOG.md, README.md and the rest of docs/ are not in the key, and they no longer say 'a stale binary is never restored'.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A test edits one compiled-in file (a prompt .md under a temp copy of the tree) and asserts the inputs digest changes. Another asserts the skip happens with a matching digest and cached binary and does not happen with a mismatched digest or no binary, and a third asserts the stamp is not left stale after a non-CI build.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p xtask` unit tests passed: the_inputs_digest_changes_when_a_compiled_in_file_is_edited (edits crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md and docs/system-facts.md in a temp tree, and each exact file), skip_only_with_ci_matching_stamp_and_binary (matching, mismatched, no binary, no stamp, no --ci), and a_non_ci_build_leaves_no_stale_stamp (stamp gone during the build, new digest after, none after a failed build).

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`. The new tests derive the compiled-in file set from include_str!/include_bytes! targets and the manifests, and fail if any athena-bin hashFiles key in ci.yml misses one. They also fail on a ci.yml variant with a restore step removed or placed after the setup step.
criteria_check.evidence: compiled_in_files() scans include literals in production code and adds the manifests and setup.sh. a_stale_or_incomplete_ci_yml_is_flagged and the_tool_cache_check_fails_when_a_restore_is_missing_or_after_setup pass. They require Err for: docs/system-facts.md removed from a key, a glob removed, the old narrower list, an uncovered compiled-in file, no key, and a restore step removed or moved after setup in each of the six jobs. The real file must give Ok.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass, including xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs and the existing policy tests.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks for the full `cargo test`. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (both clean), and `cargo test -p xtask`, which includes ci_shards.rs (20 pass) and policy.rs (17 pass).

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the gitleaks and athena binary caches, their keys, and that the speed-up on GitHub Actions is not measured here.
criteria_check.evidence: A new bullet under [Unreleased] > Changed gives the two caches, their paths, keys and the nine globs. It also covers the stamp and skip, the older-commit effect, and 'The speed-up on GitHub Actions is not measured here'.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: history does not save the caches. The plan listed saves for fmt, clippy, test and history, but history only restores, as in the rejected candidate. The same keys are saved by fmt, clippy and test on the default branch, and a fourth saver would only race on the same key. A ci.yml comment says so, and the policy test requires saves only in the three check jobs.
The digest walk and GitHub's hashFiles may differ on symlinks, but none exist under crates/ or xtask/ today. The policy test compares paths by rule, not by hash, and the ci.yml comment says so.

The include scan would miss a production include placed after an early #[cfg(test)] item, or one built with concat!. The test comment states this limit. I grepped crates/ and xtask/ and found no such form today.
Pull requests that change crates/ or xtask/ always miss the exact-only key and rebuild, because only the default branch saves. The throughput review needs to measure whether the caches help.
mistakes: My first mutant test inserted a required path under crates/ and expected it to be uncovered; crates/** covers it, so the test failed. I replaced it with a path outside the globs (docs/new-compiled-in.md) and added the crates/ case as an expected pass.
learnings: xtask is a bin-only crate, so tests in xtask/tests/ read its code by running CARGO_BIN_EXE_xtask. That is how policy.rs reads BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS.

The binary's compiled-in files are the prompts under crates/*/prompts/*.md, docs/system-facts.md (briefs.rs) and athena.toml (athena-gate/src/lib.rs BUILTIN_CONFIG). Every other include_str! in the repo is inside test code. No production include uses concat!.
The first stamp check in the rejected candidate wrote the stamp only for --ci builds. The new `rebuild_stamped` helper writes it for every build.
Bash in this environment rejects grep, tail and pipes, so output has to be read with the Read and Grep tools.
desires: A way to run `cargo test --locked` in a few minutes so the full suite could be checked before handover.
